info.title: id-proto-debugger API
info.description:
The id-proto-debugger api: a guarded proxy and relay for the protocol
workflows a browser cannot complete on its own. Every endpoint that
connects anywhere does so to a target its caller names, under the address
policy, timeouts and caps of the api's configuration.

get.description: Every operation in the API document, as a self-contained HTML page.
The API document itself: this file's output, OpenAPI 3.1.

The IANA "JSON Web Token Claims" registry, as IANA publishes it (XML),
fetched once and kept for the life of the process. The token page labels
the claims it shows from it.

post.description:
A TRANSMITTER delivers one Security Event Token (RFC 8935 section 2.1).
The body is the compact JWS, with no form encoding and no JSON wrapper.
application/jwt is accepted and recorded as the wrong type, because a
receiver that dispatched on it would drop the token with no error anybody
sees.

has every one that ran, and the sequence stops at the first whose status
is not 90xx or 61xx.

Ssf.Answer.description:
What the transmitter said. `ok` is a 2xx, and a 204 with no body is one
(`noBody`). `err` and `description` are RFC 8935 section 2.4's, which SSF
uses on every endpoint; `notJson` is the parse error of a body that is
not JSON.

url.description: The ABSOLUTE URL, from the transmitter's configuration metadata.
url.x-checked-in-code: api/ssf_proxy.js: required, and an absolute http:// or https:// URL; the address policy applies when it is called

method.description: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE, any case. Absent is GET.
method.x-checked-in-code: api/ssf_proxy.js: one of the five SSF 1.0 methods, compared upper-cased

headers.description: Header name to value; each value is sent as text, null is dropped.
headers.x-checked-in-code: api/ssf_proxy.js: each name a token, no framing or hop-by-hop header, no CR or LF in a value

body.description:
The request document: JSON, or text sent exactly as given. A DELETE
may carry one, since it names the stream it deletes.
body.x-checked-in-code: api/ssf_proxy.js: none on a GET; at most ssfMaxRequestBytes once serialised

sslValidate.description: Only false or "false" turns off certificate verification.
sslValidate.x-checked-in-code: api/ssf_proxy.js: only false or "false" turns verification off

http_trace.description: true or "true" attaches http_exchange to the answer.
http_trace.x-checked-in-code: api/server.js: only true or "true" asks for the trace

Ssf.CallRequest.description: One call to a transmitter's endpoint, as the page composed it.

deliveryEndpoint.description: This api's address as the caller reached it, plus the inbox's path.

Ssf.Created.description: A new inbox, and the URL a stream's delivery.endpoint_url takes.

from.description: The cursor actually used: `after`, clamped to 0..total.

total.description: How many pushes the inbox has ever accepted.

contentType.description: The media type the push named, lower-cased, parameters dropped.

authorization.description: Whether the push carried an Authorization header.

Ssf.Event.description:
One delivery, as it arrived. `header` and `claims` are the decoded JWS
header and payload, or null with `problem` saying why; nothing is
verified.

id.description: 32 hex digits; the inbox's whole address.

authenticated.description: Whether pushes must carry an Authorization header.

expiresAt.description: The sooner of the two expiries.

Ssf.Inbox.description: One inbox, as every receiver answer describes it.

refusedHeaderReasons.description: Each refused header, lower-cased, to why.

addressPolicyEnabled.description: Whether the address layers of the policy are on here.

Ssf.Limits.description: What the SSF proxy will and will not do, and the receiver's bounds.

held.description: How many inboxes this process holds now.

verifies.description: This service checks no signature: it holds no transmitter's key.

Ssf.ReceiverLimits.description: The push receiver's own bounds, as GET /ssf/limits reports them.

label.description: A name for the inbox, cut at 200 characters.

authorization.description:
The Authorization header every push must carry: the stream's
delivery.authorization_header. Empty is an OPEN inbox.
authorization.x-checked-in-code: api/ssf_receiver.js: at most 4096 characters once trimmed

idleTtlMs.description: How long the inbox may go unused, in ms.
idleTtlMs.x-checked-in-code: api/ssf_receiver.js: a positive whole number, at most ssfReceiverIdleTtlMs

ttlMs.description: How long the inbox lives, in ms.
ttlMs.x-checked-in-code: api/ssf_receiver.js: a positive whole number, at most ssfReceiverTtlMs

maxInboxBytes.description: How many bytes of events it holds before the oldest are dropped.
maxInboxBytes.x-checked-in-code: api/ssf_receiver.js: a positive whole number, at most ssfReceiverMaxInboxBytes and at least ssfReceiverMaxEventBytes

Ssf.ReceiverRequest.description:
A push inbox, as the page asks for one. Each of the three numbers may be
less than this service's setting of the same name, never more; absent is
that setting.

Ssf.SetError.description:
RFC 8935 section 2.4: the SET Error Code (`invalid_request`,
`authentication_failed`, ...) and the sentence that explains it.

Ssf.Unreachable.description: The transmitter could not be reached. `code` is the network error's.

wa.description: wsignin1.0, wsignout1.0, wsignoutcleanup1.0. Echoed on a sign-out.

wresult.description: The RequestSecurityTokenResponse, raw XML. Absent is a sign-out.

wctx.description: The context the relying party sent, returned as written.

WsFed.Landing.description: What the identity provider sends, in a form or a query string.

url.x-checked-in-code: api/server.js: an absolute http(s) URL (400, url must be an absolute http(s) URL.); the address is the outbound agent's

soap.description: The SOAP envelope, sent as written.

"1.1" (text/xml and a SOAPAction header) or anything else for SOAP 1.2
(the action inside application/soap+xml). Compared after String(), so
the number 1.1 is SOAP 1.1 too. Absent is 1.2.

action.description: The WS-Addressing action, into SOAPAction or the content type.

body.description: Its body as text: an RSTR, an RSTRC or a SOAP Fault.

WsTrust.StsAnswer.description: What the STS answered, whatever its status.

servers.description: The api's own origin. Embedded, it is the debugger's origin + /api.
